tc_benefit: Clients reach the vets, visits, customers and genai backends through one entry point, so services can be split, moved, renamed or replaced, and cross-cutting policy such as CircuitBreaker and Retry changed, by editing the gateway routes rather than every client.
tc_conditions: Assumes clients actually call the gateway rather than the services directly, and that backend topology or resilience policy changes over time; the benefit materialises when a route target changes or a retry/timeout policy must apply to all routes.
tc_signals: lb:// routes to vets-service, visits-service, customers-service, genai-service

tc_benefit: admin-server loads its settings from the external config server, so URLs, credentials and tuning values can change per environment or at run time by editing one place, without rebuilding or redeploying the service.
tc_conditions: Materialises when the same admin-server build runs across several environments, or when a setting must change quickly in production; assumes the config server is actually running and serving configuration at the configured URL.

tc_benefit: The api-gateway loads its settings from a central config server, so URLs, credentials and tuning values can change per environment or at run time without rebuilding or redeploying the gateway.
tc_conditions: Benefit materialises when the same gateway build runs across several environments or when routing, timeout or credential settings must change quickly in production; assumes the config server is actually deployed and reachable at the configured URL and that its own settings are managed separately.

tc_benefit: The service pulls its configuration from a central config server, so URLs, credentials and tuning values can change per environment or at run time without rebuilding or redeploying customers-service.
tc_conditions: Materialises when the same build runs across several environments or when a setting must change quickly in production; assumes the config server is actually running and reachable at the configured URL and that its repository holds per-environment config.

tc_benefit: discovery-server loads its settings from the config server rather than from its own build, so URLs, credentials and tuning values can change per environment or at run time without rebuilding the service.
tc_conditions: Materialises when the same discovery-server build runs in several environments or when a setting must change quickly in production; assumes the config server is reachable at the configured URL and that its settings are managed centrally.

tc_benefit: The service loads its configuration from a central config server, so URLs, credentials and tuning values can change per environment or at run time without rebuilding or redeploying genai-service.
tc_conditions: Materialises when the same build runs across several environments or when a setting such as a model endpoint or credential must change quickly in production; assumes the config server at config-server:8888 is actually deployed and maintained, which the snippet does not show.

tc_benefit: vets-service loads its configuration from a central config server, so settings such as URLs, credentials and tuning values can change per environment or at run time without rebuilding or redeploying the service.
tc_conditions: Benefit materialises when the same vets-service build runs across several environments or when a setting must change quickly in production; assumes the config server is actually running and reachable at the configured URL and that its repository holds the vets-service properties.
tc_signals: optional configserver with env var override CONFIG_SERVER_URL

tc_benefit: Visits-service loads its settings from a central config server, so URLs, credentials and tuning values can change per environment or at run time without rebuilding or redeploying the service.
tc_conditions: Materialises when the same build runs across several environments or when a setting must change quickly in production; assumes the config server is actually running and populated with visits-service properties at the referenced URLs.
